paper_cards.title: Gemini Robotics 2
paper_cards.data: Google DeepMind does not disclose the full training mixture; official evaluation spans humanoid whole-body control, bi-arm dexterity, cross-embodiment transfer, multi-robot collaboration, and embodied reasoning.
paper_cards.method: A VLA family comprising a cloud-scale Gemini Robotics 2 controller, an on-device variant, and Gemini Robotics ER 2 as a high-level multimodal planner that can hand off motor execution to lower-level policies.
paper_cards.task: Follow language instructions and perform dexterous, whole-body, multi-stage and coordinated physical tasks across robot forms.
paper_cards.novelty: Extends the Gemini Robotics line from arm-centric manipulation to whole-body humanoid control, cross-embodiment dexterity, local deployment and multi-robot orchestration in one official family.
paper_cards.evidence: Official launch page, capability pages, model cards and embedded videos jointly document the system boundary, supported inputs and demonstrated tasks.

claim_checks.claim: Released July 30, 2026 with whole-body and advanced dexterity capabilities
ER 2 accepts interleaved text/image/video/audio with up to 128k context

claim_checks.notes: Access is product/trusted-tester oriented; no open weights claimed.

paper_cards.limitations: Closed weights and undisclosed training mixture limit reproducibility; official demos are curated and do not expose full failure distributions.
paper_cards.project_relevance: High-value system reference for hierarchical VLA/ER decomposition, whole-body action interfaces, cross-embodiment evaluation and multi-agent robot coordination.

paper_cards.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
paper_cards.data: Heterogeneous OXE robot video, DROID, Bridge, bimanual YAM, G1 humanoid and egocentric human video are unified through end-effector, language and learned latent-action conditioning.
paper_cards.method: A two-stage curriculum first learns physical priors from unlabeled cross-embodiment video using latent actions, then grounds the model in end-effector action spaces for zero-shot deployment and few-shot adaptation.
paper_cards.task: Predict action-conditioned robot futures across embodiments and use those rollouts for planning, evaluation and policy improvement.
paper_cards.novelty: Treats shared physical laws rather than robot-specific controls as the transferable substrate, reconciling action spaces with three complementary interfaces.
paper_cards.evidence: The arXiv paper, official project and public repository provide code, checkpoints, dataset registry, offline evaluation and policy-in-the-loop deployment instructions.

claim_checks.notes: Repository documents checkpoints and end-to-end commands.

claim_checks.claim: Cross-embodiment coverage includes DROID, Bridge, bimanual YAM and G1

paper_cards.limitations: Generated rollouts can still contain physical hallucinations; full OXE-scale training is expensive and source datasets are not bundled.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct world-action reference for universal action schemas, cross-embodiment dynamics, learned simulator interfaces and policy-in-the-loop validation.

paper_cards.title: SpatialCrafter: Single Image World Modeling with Generative 3D Proxies
paper_cards.data: Single-image indoor and outdoor scenes, camera trajectories and long video sequences; the official page shows diverse exploration examples and long-horizon generation.
paper_cards.method: A two-stage pipeline first predicts a point-anchored sparse global 3D proxy with PaSS Flow, then refines appearance with a video diffusion model while retaining proxy-based spatial memory.
paper_cards.task: Turn one image into a controllable, explorable scene and synthesize camera-conditioned videos that remain consistent over long trajectories.
paper_cards.novelty: Uses a generative global 3D proxy as persistent geometry and memory, reducing drift and hallucination relative to sparse-point or panorama conditioning.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper and official SIGGRAPH Asia project page expose indoor/outdoor galleries, long-video results and method overview.

claim_checks.notes: Official project and author publication page.

claim_checks.claim: Global 3D proxy supports long chunked generation

claim_checks.notes: Official page still marks code and Hugging Face as TBA.

paper_cards.limitations: No released code or checkpoints at review time; appearance refinement remains video-based rather than a queryable physics state.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong reference for persistent 3D memory, controllable camera trajectories and separating structural proxy generation from photorealistic rendering.

paper_cards.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
paper_cards.data: 50 scenarios across eight physical-mechanism groups, split into 25 calibration cases with reference probabilities and 25 coverage cases with enumerable valid outcomes.
paper_cards.method: Repeated rollouts are mapped to terminal outcomes; support alignment and probability-mass alignment are measured separately, with language, noise and fine-tuning probes for distribution shaping.
paper_cards.task: Evaluate whether a stochastic video world model represents which physical futures are possible and assigns them appropriate probabilities.
paper_cards.novelty: Moves world-model evaluation from one plausible rollout to the induced distribution over possible futures.
paper_cards.evidence: Official project page, arXiv paper, code/benchmark links, diagrams and eleven-model diagnosis provide primary evidence.

claim_checks.claim: No evaluated model jointly achieves calibration, support and scene reliability

paper_cards.limitations: Terminal-outcome abstraction does not measure full trajectory distributions; only half the scenarios have reference probabilities.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Provides explicit PossibleOutcome, OutcomeProbability, SupportCoverage and CalibrationError fields for stochastic physical-world evaluation.

paper_cards.title: R2M-Bench: Evaluating Revisit Memory via Relative Consistency in Interactive Video World Models
paper_cards.data: 100 reference scenes with three leave-and-return trajectories each, producing 300 instances across appearance, identity, local geometry and persistent-state criteria.
paper_cards.method: Each revisit is compared against gap-matched non-revisit and short-range controls to compute MemoryGain and Normalized Memory Ratio, separating memory from generic temporal stability or failed motion.
paper_cards.task: Measure whether interactive video world models preserve scene state after leaving and returning rather than exploiting slow or static rollouts.
paper_cards.novelty: Introduces same-rollout relative calibration that explicitly discounts the slow-motion shortcut in revisit-consistency scores.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary arXiv paper documents the dataset, metrics, seven-model comparison, human-correlation study and failure analysis.

claim_checks.claim: 300 instances from 100 scenes and three trajectories
Overall NMR has Spearman rho 0.547 with human consistency judgments

paper_cards.limitations: No separate official code/project page was located; benchmark scale is modest and focuses on revisit memory rather than full interactive competence.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct metric reference for persistent world state, return-to-location consistency and shortcut-resistant long-horizon evaluation.

paper_cards.title: 4DSynth: Controllable Procedural World Synthesis for Dynamic Embodied Simulation
paper_cards.data: Procedurally generated dynamic scenes and 4DSynth-Nav navigation tasks across three difficulty tiers.
paper_cards.method: Converts text, blueprint masks or a photograph into explicit geometry, animated actors, collision-free trajectories and physics-ready state sharing a geometry-grounded representation.
paper_cards.task: Create editable 4D simulation environments and reproducible embodied navigation tasks.
paper_cards.novelty: Unifies procedural scene generation, dynamic actors, camera planning, rendering and task generation in one controllable representation.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper supports the architecture and benchmark claims, but no inspectable official project/gallery was located.

claim_checks.claim: 4DSynth-Nav evaluates two VLMs across three tiers

paper_cards.limitations: Visual diversity, collision quality, trajectory realism and simulator import behavior cannot be judged confidently without an official gallery/demo.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Excellent direct fit for editable dynamic world state and task generation, pending visual review.

paper_cards.title: Riemann-1.0: An Embodied World Action Model for Physical AI
paper_cards.data: Reported 200K+ hours combining egocentric human video, handheld-gripper demonstrations and heterogeneous robot trajectories.
paper_cards.method: Fully causal autoregressive modeling of multi-view observations, robot states and embodiment-specific actions, with progressive pretraining across increasingly action-grounded data.
paper_cards.task: Serve as both an executable robot policy and a multi-embodiment visual world simulator.
paper_cards.novelty: Unifies causal policy execution and action-conditioned world simulation rather than coupling separate policy and predictor modules.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper supports architecture, scale and reported benchmark results; no sufficiently inspectable official release/demo surface was found.

claim_checks.notes: Author-reported; data composition not independently audited.

paper_cards.limitations: Extraordinary scale and benchmark claims are not independently reproduced; real-robot diversity and failures cannot be assessed from an official demo surface.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct reference for a single causal world-action interface, pending human visual and release review.

paper_cards.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
paper_cards.data: RoboTwin and real-robot expert/off-expert action trajectories used to diagnose action adherence and policy-improvement utility.
paper_cards.method: WorldEcho evaluates visual integrity and SE(3) trajectory alignment across broader actions; WorldSync expands action consequences, adds an Action-Forcing Expert and aligns intervention effects.
paper_cards.task: Test and improve whether generated robot futures actually follow commanded actions, including off-expert controls.
paper_cards.novelty: Separates action-following reliability from visual plausibility and explicitly evaluates intervention consistency outside expert demonstrations.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper supports the method and reported policy-improvement findings; no inspectable official project/demo surface was located.

claim_checks.claim: Current world models fail on diverse off-expert trajectories

claim_checks.notes: Author-reported on RoboTwin and real robot.

paper_cards.limitations: Physical and generated failure cases require visual inspection; release status is unclear.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct evaluator for ActionCondition, InterventionEffect, TrajectoryAlignment and generated-simulator reliability.
